---
title: "DML refit demo"
output: html_document
---

Use the updated local package (0.2.2.9011 or later).

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(error = FALSE)
library(did)
library(dml.sensemakr)
```

1. Fit the original DiD model. If you already have `fit`, start at step 2.

```{r}
data("mpdta", package = "did")
fit <- did::att_gt(
  data = mpdta, yname = "lemp", tname = "year",
  idname = "countyreal", gname = "first.treat", xformla = ~ lpop,
  panel = TRUE, est_method = "dr", control_group = "nevertreated",
  bstrap = FALSE, cband = FALSE, compute_inffunc = FALSE
)
```

2. Reestimate ATT and both sensitivity moments by DML.

```{r}
m <- dml_from_did(
  fit, group = 2007, time = 2007, method = "dml_refit",
  dml_args = list(yreg = "lm", dreg = "glm", d.class = TRUE,
                  cf.folds = 5, cf.seed = 1)
)
summary(m)
unlist(m$results$main$treat[[1]]$estimates[c("theta.s", "sigma2.s", "nu2.s")])
```

`lm` and `glm` are simple example nuisance learners; the three parameters use
cross-fitted DML scores. The ATT can differ from `fit$att`. Equal sampling weights
are required. Active DML propensity clipping stops the fit.

3. Run sensitivity analysis or pre-trend benchmarking.

```{r}
confidence_bounds(m, cf.y = 0.05, cf.d = 0.05)
b <- did_pretrend_bounds(
  m, pre_period = c(2005, 2006), k = c(0, 0.5, 1, 2),
  type = "bias", level = 0.975
)
b
```

The placebo is also estimated by DML on the same units and folds. Pre-trend
bounds require a zero pre-period causal effect and the chosen bias-transport
restriction; delta inference at positive `k` requires a nonzero population
placebo ATT. `cf.reps` and optional `dirty.tuning = TRUE` go in `dml_args`.
